name: Keliko
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Tucker, A. N. 1940. The Eastern Sudanic Languages (Keliko section, ~7pp); archive.org copy is lending-restricted. Also Waag 2018 (grammar of space, not phonology).

sources.citation: Boone, Douglas W. & Richard L. Watson (eds.). 1999. Moru-Ma'di survey report. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 1999-001. 260 pp.
sources.note: Survey (wordlists, intelligibility, sociolinguistics). 'Tone was noted on the Kaliko lists'; Kaliko cluster = Sudanese Kaliko, Kaliko-Ma'di (Didi, Dogo; DRC) and Kaliko-Omi (DRC). grep stress/accent over the whole report: no prosodic hits. Bibliography cites Goyvaerts 1985[=1986] and Goyvaerts 1986b 'A Kaliko text with grammatical notes and comments'.

sources.citation: Goyvaerts, Didier L. 1986. Some aspects of Kaliko phonology and morphology. Africana Linguistica 10: 43-53. Tervuren: MRAC. DOI 10.3406/aflin.1986.926
sources.note: Sec. 2.3 'Prosody' (p. 48) is tone only: four contrastive tones, Low, Mid, High and a marginal Rising; sec. 2.4 syllable CV; sec. 3 vowel deletion creates LH and marginal HL contours. The words stress/accent do not occur in the article (Persee in-document scanned search = 0 hits; own scanned grep = 0 hits). Data from one speaker of the Kaliko of Ombatse (3.18N 30.40E, 70 km N of Aru, DRC), fieldwork Oct 1983.

sources.citation: Tucker, A. N. & M. A. Bryan. 1966. Linguistic Analyses: The Non-Bantu Languages of North-Eastern Africa. London: OUP for IAI. Ch. 'The Moru-Mangbetu languages', sec. 2b Stress, p. 31.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Old Widener 2235.4.26; LIN GEN CoPh 36.88 (also: publisher (doi, likely paywalled))
sources.harvard_location: WID Old Widener 2235.4.26; LIN GEN CoPh 36.88
sources.note: Group-level only: 'In MORU stress is on the first syllable of disyllabic words... In MA'DI, however, stress is on the final vowel'; 'No such uniformity of stress pattern... has been found in the other Language Groups.' Keliko is not named in the stress section (the tone section names Moru, Ma'di, Logo, Lugbara).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 reference list for keli1248 (8 entries: Waag 2018; Tucker 1940; Boone & Watson 1999; Nalder 1937 ethnographic survey; two 2002 SIL Keliko primers; Kilpatrick 2004; Alo 1973) and PHOIBLE inventory 1339 'Kaliko (GM)' (source Goyvaerts 1986; three tones, no stress)
sources.note: Bibliographic only; no further descriptive works on Keliko phonology exist in Glottolog beyond those listed above.

sources.citation: Kilpatrick, Eileen. 2004. Orthographies of Moru-Ma'di languages. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 9: 85-91. Entebbe: SIL-Sudan.
sources.note: p. 88 'Tones': 'All Moru-Madi languages have three level tones, High, Mid and Low.... Wadi, Keliko, Madi and Keliko have falling tone on short vowels.' Keliko grapheme column in every chart (nine vowels, labio-velar nasal, no labialized consonants). No mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Waag, Christine. 2018. The grammar of space in Keliko, a Central Sudanic language of South Sudan. In H. Schroder & P. Jerono (eds.), Nilo-Saharan Issues and Perspectives, 193-209. Koln: Rudiger Koppe.

sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: archive.org copy (easternsudanicla0001tuck) is access-restricted; only scanned snippets via Open Library search-inside. Keliko appears in comparative morphology (plural particle -ki, linking particle ve) and ch. III 'Intonation' treats three level tones with Moru (Miza) as representative. An earlier reader enumerated every scanned hit for stress/stressed/accent in the volume: none concerns Keliko or any Moru-Ma'di stress rule. Goyvaerts 1986: 52 calls Tucker's Kaliko remarks 'a few scattered and... not always very reliable remarks'.
